summary: The article surveys photographers and researchers who pursue folkloric creatures and cryptids, including Bigfoot, Nessie, the chupacabra, the Mothman, the Wendigo, the Yeti and Chinese dragons, each tied to recent reported sightings in 2023-2024. It argues that their motivations go beyond proving the creatures exist, and instead explore the intersection of mythology, culture and the modern world.
one_line: Photographers and scholars chase Bigfoot, Nessie, the chupacabra, Mothman, Wendigo, Yeti and dragons, exploring folklore and culture more than proving existence.
key_facts: A grainy video by hikers in the Washington Cascades went viral on September 4, 2023, rekindling the hunt for Bigfoot (Sasquatch).
Anthropologist Dr. Emily Carter argues Bigfoot is an integral part of Native American lore and represents humanity's deep connection to nature.
Photographer James "Jim" Collins suggests Bigfoot is a symbol of the wilderness that modern society is rapidly losing.
A claimed Loch Ness Monster sighting on October 22, 2023 renewed global interest in Nessie.
Underwater photographer Alex Thompson uses submersible drones to explore Loch Ness in search of photographic evidence of Nessie.
Marine biologist Dr. Fiona MacGregor says Nessie embodies Scotland's natural mysteries and the cultural pride of its people.
The chupacabra is described as a reptile-like creature with greenish-gray skin and spines down its back that drinks the blood of livestock, especially goats.
After a surge in reported cattle attacks near Puerto Rico in late November 2023, wildlife photographer Maria Sanchez spent months setting camera traps in Puerto Rico's forests.
On November 12, 2023, the latest Mothman sighting was reported in Point Pleasant, West Virginia; the winged, red-eyed figure is said to be an omen of disaster.
Documentarian Robert Peterson has spent years photographing Point Pleasant and argues the Mothman is a living element of the town's identity.

After a Wendigo sighting report on December 1, 2023, First Nations leaders like Michael Two-bears invited scholars and photographers to record and respect their traditions; photographer Hannah Lewis uses stark landscapes.
After unverified Yeti tracks were found in spring 2024, tracker Tenzin Sherpa and photographer Sarah Jennings collaborated to document the creature in the Himalayas.
Throughout 2023, reports from China's remote mountains claimed dragon sightings; historian Li Ming sees them as vital to Chinese mythology, and photographers use drones to survey the mountains.
